name: NEET UG
approxCandidates: ≈22–23 lakh candidates (over 22 lakh appeared in the June 2026 re-exam)
eligibility: Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology and English (50% PCB for General, 40% SC/ST/OBC); minimum age 17 by 31 Dec of admission year; no upper age limit

notification.summary: NEET UG 2026 held on 3 May 2026 was cancelled by NTA after a confirmed paper leak; a pen-and-paper re-exam was held on 21 June 2026 (over 22 lakh appeared) with results in July 2026. For 2027 the Union Education Ministry has announced a shift to computer-based testing, but the final format, shifts/normalisation and the information bulletin were still awaited as of 10 Oct 2026.

pattern.notes: Since 2025 all 180 questions are compulsory (the optional Section B was dropped) and the duration is 180 minutes. If NEET 2027 moves to multi-shift CBT, NTA has indicated scores would be normalised across shifts.

trendAnalysis.summary: Biology (90 questions) is overwhelmingly NCERT-line based, with genetics, molecular biology, human physiology, reproduction and ecology the highest-yield areas and a growing share of statement-based, match-the-column and assertion–reason items. Physics swung from moderate (2024) to the toughest section (2025, lengthy numericals in electrostatics, current electricity, optics and modern physics). Chemistry is moderate: physical chemistry numericals plus NCERT-text inorganic (bonding, coordination, p-block) and reaction-based organic. Cut-offs fell sharply in 2025 as difficulty rose; the 2026 re-exam was reported as moderate.

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from NTA's officially released NEET (UG) question papers and final answer keys for 2024 and 2025 and the 2026 paper, as summarised in public subject-wise analyses (Physics Wallah, Careers360, Vedantu chapter tables). Web search confirmed the format mix (≈66% direct MCQs, plus Statement I/II, multi-statement, assertion–reason and match-the-list items concentrated in Biology and Chemistry; Physics almost entirely numerical/direct MCQs). Full papers could not be fetched, so concept + format + trap patterns were written from the drafter's own knowledge of these papers and the NCERT (rationalised) syllabus. The blueprint is larger than usual because NEET has 180 questions spread over 75 chapters.

archetypes.pattern: Identify pairs of quantities with the same dimensions or the dimension of a constant; distractors differ in one exponent
Equations of uniformly accelerated motion and v–t graphs: distance, time or acceleration in one step
Apparent weight in an accelerating lift / Newton’s second law with simple forces
Block pulled on a rough surface or connected blocks: acceleration with kinetic friction
Spring/gravitational energy converted to kinetic energy; work–energy theorem
Moment of inertia via parallel/perpendicular-axis theorem for rods, rings, discs
Rolling bodies: ratio of rotational to total kinetic energy, angular momentum conservation
Change in g with radius/height/depth; percentage change approximations
Escape/orbital speed scaling with planet mass and radius; Kepler’s third law
Young’s modulus: extension scaling with length and radius for the same material/load
Terminal velocity (Stokes’ law), surface tension excess pressure, Bernoulli/continuity
Carnot engine efficiency and source/sink temperature changes
First law in isothermal/adiabatic/isochoric processes — which of ΔU, Q, W is zero or equal
rms speed and mean kinetic energy scaling with temperature and molar mass
Simple pendulum/spring period change when length, mass or g changes
Wave equation y = A sin(ωt − kx): speed, wavelength, frequency; strings and pipes
Coulomb force after charge sharing by touching identical spheres
Capacitor combinations, energy stored, field/potential of point charges and dipoles
Metre bridge / Wheatstone bridge balance for unknown resistance
Cell with internal resistance: current, terminal voltage, power; series–parallel networks
Magnetic field at the centre of a circular coil or due to a straight wire
Galvanometer conversion to ammeter/voltmeter; force on charges/wires; magnetic materials
Average power and power factor in LR/LCR AC circuits
Transformers, induced emf from changing flux, self/mutual inductance
Order of EM spectrum and properties/uses of radiations
Mirror/lens formula: position and nature of image
Lens combinations and power, prism, TIR, optical instruments magnification
YDSE fringe width, diffraction width, polarisation (Malus’ law, Brewster angle)
Photoelectric equation, stopping potential, de Broglie wavelength comparisons
Radioactive decay: fraction remaining/decayed after n half-lives
Bohr model radius/energy ratios, spectral series, binding energy
Rectifier output frequency, diode biasing and characteristics
Logic gates: identify gate or output from truth table/combination
Mole concept: number of atoms/molecules, mass of given moles, molarity
Validity of quantum-number sets; orbitals and electrons for given quantum numbers
Bohr model energies/radii and de Broglie/uncertainty principle calculations
Ordering of ionisation enthalpy, electronegativity, atomic/ionic radii
Hybridisation and shape (VSEPR) of a molecule/ion; match species with shapes
Order of bond angles or dipole moments in a series of molecules
MOT: bond order and magnetic character of diatomic species
Hess’s law: enthalpy of formation from combustion data
Spontaneity from signs of ΔH and ΔS; ΔH − ΔU; entropy changes
Ksp and molar solubility of sparingly soluble salts (AB, AB₂, A₂B types)
pH of very dilute acids, buffers and salt solutions; often assertion–reason
Oxidation number (including average/fractional values) and identification of redox reactions
Colligative properties with van’t Hoff factor: compare boiling/freezing points of solutions
Faraday’s laws, Nernst equation, molar conductivity trends
Effect of concentration changes on rate from rate law
First-order half-life: fraction remaining, time for given completion; Arrhenius
Trends in group 15/16 hydrides (reducing power, stability, basicity)
Structures of oxoacids of S/P and bonds present (S–S, O–O, P–H)
Consequences of lanthanoid contraction; properties of lanthanoids/actinoids
Spin-only magnetic moment, colour and oxidation states of 3d ions
Isomerism (geometrical/optical) of complexes
Ligand denticity, hybridisation, magnetic nature, CFSE and nomenclature
Order of acidic/basic strength from inductive and resonance effects
Purification techniques and qualitative analysis; IUPAC names and isomerism
Markovnikov vs peroxide-effect addition of HBr; ozonolysis products
Aromaticity (Hückel 4n + 2) and electrophilic substitution of benzene
Named reactions (Finkelstein, Swarts, Wurtz, Sandmeyer) and SN1/SN2 reactivity
Acidity of alcohols/phenols, preparation and reactions (Williamson, Lucas, Kolbe)
Reduction/oxidation conversions (Clemmensen, Wolff–Kishner) and named reactions
Iodoform/Tollens’/Fehling’s tests and acidity of carboxylic acids
Basicity order of amines in aqueous solution
Tests and reactions of amines (carbylamine, Hinsberg, diazotisation)
Reactions/structure of glucose, sugars, proteins, vitamins and nucleic acids
Distinctive features of Monera/Protista/Fungi groups (mycoplasma, cyanobacteria, fungal classes)
Plant kingdom: dominant phase and life cycles of algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms
Taxonomic categories, nomenclature rules and taxonomic aids
Identify monocot/dicot stem/root from vascular bundle and tissue features
Secondary growth: cambium products, periderm, bark, heartwood/sapwood
Placentation, aestivation and floral features with examples
Family characters (Fabaceae, Solanaceae, Liliaceae) and floral formulae
Organelles with DNA/70S ribosomes; prokaryotic vs eukaryotic features
Composition and structure of plasma membrane and other organelles (NCERT numbers)
Match-the-list: organelle with function
Events of meiosis/mitosis stages (crossing over, synapsis, chiasmata)
Chromosome number and DNA content (C value) in different phases
ATP/NADPH counts in Calvin cycle; light-reaction products
C₄ pathway (PEP, OAA, Kranz anatomy) and photorespiration
Counts of CO₂/NADH/ATP in glycolysis and Krebs cycle; respiratory quotient
Functions of plant growth regulators (bolting, apical dominance, senescence)
Number of meiotic divisions for pollen/seeds; embryo sac structure and ploidy
Genotype/phenotype proportions in di-/tri-hybrid crosses and test crosses
Multiple alleles (ABO), incomplete dominance and codominance outcomes
Sex-linked inheritance (colour blindness, haemophilia) and pedigree probabilities
Chargaff’s rule: base percentages and hydrogen-bond counts
Transcription machinery (RNA polymerases), lac operon components, genetic code
Classic experiments (Meselson–Stahl, Hershey–Chase, Griffith) and their results
Population interactions (mutualism, commensalism, amensalism…) and growth models
10 per cent law energy transfer through trophic levels
Ecological pyramids, productivity, decomposition and succession facts
Causes of biodiversity loss and in-situ/ex-situ conservation examples
Phylum-level features: circulatory system type, symmetry, germ layers
Coelom types (acoelomate/pseudocoelomate/coelomate) with examples
Animal tissues: epithelium types and locations; frog morphology/anatomy
Enzyme inhibition and kinetics
Structure of biomolecules: bonds in nucleotides, proteins and polysaccharides
Lung volumes and capacities
Transport of O₂ and CO₂ (percentages, dissociation curve)
ECG waves and cardiac cycle events
Cardiac output, blood groups, double circulation
Regulation of kidney function (RAAS, ANF, ADH)
Statement I/II or multi-statement format; permeability and function of nephron segments
Sliding-filament theory: bands that change during contraction; joints and skeletal disorders
Resting/action potential ion permeability; structure of eye and ear
Source gland of a hormone; hormone deficiency/excess disorders
Gametogenesis counts (ova/sperms from primary oocytes/spermatocytes)
Menstrual cycle hormones, ovulation, fertilisation and embryonic development
Contraceptive methods, STIs and ART techniques
Homologous vs analogous organs; evidence of evolution; origin of life experiments
Hardy–Weinberg allele and genotype frequency calculations
Pathogen life cycles (Plasmodium) and disease–pathogen matching
Immunity: antibody types, active/passive immunity, vaccines
Cloning vectors (pBR322 markers, insertional inactivation), restriction enzymes
PCR, gel electrophoresis, bioreactors and downstream processing
Bt crops (cry genes), RNAi, transgenic animals, gene therapy
Microbe–product/use matching (antibiotics, enzymes, biogas, biofertilisers)

resources.notes: NTA releases the test-booklet codes' question papers with provisional and final answer keys on neet.nta.nic.in (and exams.nta.ac.in/NEET) after each exam; candidates see their OMR/response sheets during the challenge window. No dedicated official full-length mock is currently published; if the 2027 exam moves to CBT, NTA is expected to post a practice CBT.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of physical quantities have the same dimensions?
questions.explanation: Work = force × displacement and torque = force × lever arm both have dimensions ML²T⁻².

relevance.note: Work/torque same dimensions – frequent NEET one-liner with near-miss pairs

questions.question: A person of mass 60 kg stands on a weighing scale in a lift moving downward with an acceleration of 2 m/s². The scale reads (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Apparent weight = m(g − a) = 60 × (10 − 2) = 480 N.

relevance.note: Lift moving down with a, scale 480 N – NEET staple with 600/720 distractors

questions.question: A spring of spring constant 200 N/m is compressed by 10 cm and used to launch a 0.5 kg block on a smooth horizontal surface. The speed of the block on leaving the spring is
questions.explanation: ½kx² = ½mv² ⇒ v = x√(k/m) = 0.1 × √400 = 2 m/s.

relevance.note: Spring PE → KE speed 2 m/s; NEET-level numeric, cm→m trap

questions.question: The moment of inertia of a thin uniform rod of mass M and length L about an axis perpendicular to it through a point at distance L/4 from one end is
questions.explanation: Parallel-axis theorem: I = ML²/12 + M(L/4)² = ML²/12 + ML²/16 = 7ML²/48.

relevance.note: Rod MI about L/4 point 7ML²/48 – classic NEET parallel-axis item

questions.question: A wire extends by 1 mm under a certain load. Another wire of the same material, with twice the length and twice the radius, is subjected to the same load. Its extension is
questions.explanation: ΔL = FL/(πr²Y) ∝ L/r². New ΔL = 1 mm × 2/4 = 0.5 mm.

relevance.note: Extension ∝ L/r² → 0.5 mm; NEET PYQ pattern

questions.question: A Carnot engine has an efficiency of 40% with its sink at 300 K. The temperature of the source is

relevance.note: Carnot source T from η and sink, 500 K – NEET staple

questions.question: The length of a simple pendulum is increased by 21%. Its time period increases by
questions.explanation: T ∝ √L, so T' = T√1.21 = 1.1T, an increase of 10%.

relevance.note: Pendulum length +21% → T +10% – recurring NEET item

questions.question: Two identical small conducting spheres carrying equal charges repel each other with force F. A third identical uncharged sphere is touched first to one sphere, then to the other, and removed. The new force between the first two spheres (same separation) is
questions.explanation: Charges become q/2 on the first; the third then has q/2 and shares with the second: (q/2 + q)/2 = 3q/4. Force ∝ (q/2)(3q/4) = 3q²/8 ⇒ 3F/8.

relevance.note: Third sphere touching both → 3F/8, exact NEET PYQ type

questions.question: In a metre bridge, a null point is found at 40 cm from the left end when an unknown resistance X is in the left gap and 12 Ω is in the right gap. The value of X is

relevance.note: Metre bridge balance X = 8 Ω with 18 Ω inverse distractor – NEET style

questions.question: A circular coil of 100 turns and radius 10 cm carries a current of 1 A. The magnetic field at its centre is approximately (μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T m A⁻¹)

relevance.note: Coil field μ0NI/2r = 6.28e-4 T; standard NEET

questions.question: A resistor of 30 Ω and an inductor of reactance 40 Ω are connected in series to a 200 V (rms) AC supply. The average power dissipated is

relevance.note: LR average power I²R = 480 W with V²/R distractor – NEET style

questions.question: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm. The image formed is
options: Real, inverted, 60 cm in front of the mirror, magnified 2 times
Virtual, erect, 60 cm behind the mirror, magnified 2 times
Real, inverted, 12 cm in front of the mirror, diminished
Real, erect, 60 cm in front of the mirror, magnified 3 times
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/20 + 1/30 = −1/60 ⇒ v = −60 cm (real, in front). m = −v/u = −2 ⇒ inverted, twice the size.

relevance.note: Concave mirror image nature/position; NEET-level

questions.question: After three half-lives, the fraction of a radioactive sample that has decayed is
questions.explanation: Remaining = (1/2)³ = 1/8, so decayed = 1 − 1/8 = 7/8.

relevance.note: Fraction decayed after 3 half-lives 7/8 vs 1/8 trap; NEET-level easy

questions.question: A full-wave rectifier is fed with 50 Hz AC mains. The fundamental frequency of the ripple in its output is
questions.explanation: A full-wave rectifier gives one output pulse for each half cycle, so the ripple frequency is 2 × 50 = 100 Hz.

relevance.note: Full-wave ripple 100 Hz – NEET repeated one-liner

questions.question: If the Earth were to shrink so that its radius decreased by 1% with its mass unchanged, the acceleration due to gravity at its surface would

relevance.note: Radius −1% → g +2%; NEET percentage-approximation item

questions.question: The total number of atoms present in 0.1 mol of methane (CH₄) is (N_A = 6.022 × 10²³)
questions.explanation: Each CH₄ has 5 atoms: 0.1 × 5 = 0.5 mol of atoms = 0.5 × 6.022 × 10²³ = 3.011 × 10²³.

relevance.note: Atoms in 0.1 mol CH4 with molecule-count trap – NEET-level

questions.question: Which set of quantum numbers is NOT permissible for an electron?
questions.explanation: l can only take values 0 to n − 1; for n = 2, l = 2 is not allowed.

relevance.note: Invalid quantum number set (l = n) – NEET staple

questions.question: The hybridisation of the central atom and the shape of ClF₃ are
questions.explanation: Cl has 3 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs (5 electron domains, sp³d). Lone pairs occupy equatorial positions, giving a T-shape.

relevance.note: ClF3 sp3d T-shaped – frequent NEET VSEPR item

questions.question: Given ΔcH° of CH₄ = −890.3, ΔfH° of CO₂ = −393.5 and ΔfH° of H₂O(l) = −285.8 kJ mol⁻¹. The standard enthalpy of formation of CH₄ is

relevance.note: ΔfH of CH4 from combustion data −74.8 – classic NEET Hess

questions.question: The solubility product of Ag₂CrO₄ is 3.2 × 10⁻¹¹ at 25 °C. Its molar solubility in water is
questions.explanation: Ag₂CrO₄ ⇌ 2Ag⁺ + CrO₄²⁻: Ksp = (2s)²s = 4s³ ⇒ s³ = 8 × 10⁻¹² ⇒ s = 2 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹.

relevance.note: Ag2CrO4 solubility 4s³ = Ksp → 2e-4 – NEET A2B type

questions.question: For the rate law r = k[A]²[B], if [A] is doubled and [B] is halved, the rate becomes

relevance.note: Rate law [A]²[B] scaling ×2 – NEET-level

questions.question: Among the hydrides of group 15, the strongest reducing agent is
questions.explanation: Down the group the E–H bond becomes weaker, so reducing character increases: NH₃ < PH₃ < AsH₃ < SbH₃ < BiH₃.

relevance.note: BiH3 strongest reducing hydride; NEET trend item

questions.question: A direct consequence of lanthanoid contraction is that
options: Lanthanoids show only the +2 oxidation state
Atomic size increases from La to Lu
Zr and Hf have almost identical atomic radii
Basic strength of hydroxides increases from La(OH)₃ to Lu(OH)₃
questions.explanation: Poor shielding by 4f electrons makes 5d elements nearly the same size as 4d ones (Zr 160 pm, Hf 159 pm). Radii decrease and basicity decreases across the series; +3 is the common state.

relevance.note: Zr/Hf similar radii as consequence of lanthanoid contraction – NEET favourite

questions.question: Which of the following complexes shows optical isomerism?
questions.explanation: cis-[Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺ has no plane of symmetry and exists as a pair of enantiomers. The trans isomer, the homoleptic complex and the square-planar Pt complex have mirror planes.

relevance.note: cis-[Co(en)2Cl2]+ optically active – NEET staple

questions.question: The correct order of acidic strength is
questions.explanation: Each Cl exerts an −I effect that stabilises the carboxylate ion; more Cl atoms give a stronger acid. CH₃ (+I) makes acetic acid the weakest.

relevance.note: Chloroacetic acid acidity order; NEET-level

questions.question: Propene reacts with HBr in the presence of benzoyl peroxide. The major product is
questions.explanation: In the presence of peroxide, HBr adds by a free-radical mechanism (Kharasch effect), giving the anti-Markovnikov product CH₃CH₂CH₂Br.

relevance.note: Peroxide effect gives 1-bromopropane – NEET staple

questions.question: Acetophenone can be converted directly into ethylbenzene by
questions.explanation: Clemmensen reduction (Zn–Hg/conc. HCl) reduces C=O to CH₂. LiAlH₄ and NaBH₄ give the secondary alcohol; Pd–BaSO₄ (Rosenmund catalyst) does not reduce the ketone to the alkane.

relevance.note: Clemmensen reduction reagent – NEET-level

questions.question: The correct order of basic strength of the following in aqueous solution is
questions.explanation: In water, basicity depends on +I effect, solvation and steric hindrance; for ethyl amines the order is 2° > 3° > 1° > NH₃ (NCERT).

relevance.note: Ethylamine series aqueous basicity 2°>3°>1° – NEET trap (differs from methyl)

questions.question: On prolonged heating with HI, glucose gives
questions.explanation: Prolonged heating with HI reduces glucose to n-hexane, showing its six carbons are in a straight chain.

relevance.note: Glucose + HI → n-hexane, NCERT line NEET repeatedly asks

questions.question: Which organisms lack a cell wall and are the smallest living cells known that can survive without oxygen?
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma completely lacks a cell wall, is the smallest known living cell and can survive without oxygen.

relevance.note: Mycoplasma NCERT descriptor – NEET-faithful

questions.question: Conjoint, collateral, closed vascular bundles scattered in the ground tissue and surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath are characteristic of
questions.explanation: Monocot stems have numerous scattered, closed (no cambium) conjoint collateral bundles with sclerenchymatous sheaths; roots have radial bundles and dicot stems have bundles in a ring.

relevance.note: Monocot stem vascular bundle features – NEET anatomy

questions.question: Marginal placentation is found in
questions.explanation: In pea (Fabaceae) the ovules are borne along the ventral suture of a single-chambered ovary (marginal). Mustard has parietal, sunflower basal and Dianthus free-central placentation.

relevance.note: Marginal placentation pea – NEET staple

questions.question: Which of the following cell organelles contains its own DNA and 70S ribosomes?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts (and mitochondria) are semi-autonomous: they have circular DNA and 70S ribosomes.

relevance.note: Chloroplast own DNA/70S; NEET-level, slightly easy

questions.question: According to NCERT, the membrane of the human erythrocyte has approximately
questions.explanation: Biochemical studies of human RBC membranes show about 52 per cent protein and 40 per cent lipids.

relevance.note: Erythrocyte membrane 52% protein 40% lipid – NCERT number NEET asks

questions.question: Crossing over between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes takes place during
questions.explanation: Synapsis occurs in zygotene; exchange of segments (crossing over, aided by recombinase) occurs in pachytene; chiasmata become visible in diplotene.

relevance.note: Crossing over at pachytene – NEET staple

questions.question: To produce one molecule of glucose through the Calvin cycle, the number of ATP and NADPH molecules required is
questions.explanation: Each CO₂ fixed needs 3 ATP and 2 NADPH; six turns (6 CO₂) for one glucose need 18 ATP and 12 NADPH.

relevance.note: 18 ATP + 12 NADPH per glucose – NEET staple

questions.question: How many molecules of CO₂ are released in one turn of the Krebs cycle (oxidation of one acetyl CoA)?
questions.explanation: Decarboxylation occurs at isocitrate → α-ketoglutarate and α-ketoglutarate → succinyl CoA: 2 CO₂ per acetyl CoA (the third CO₂ per pyruvate is released in the link reaction).

relevance.note: 2 CO2 per Krebs turn; NEET count item

questions.question: How many meiotic divisions are needed to produce 100 pollen grains?
questions.explanation: Each microspore mother cell undergoes one meiosis to form a tetrad of four pollen grains: 100/4 = 25.

relevance.note: 25 meioses for 100 pollen – NEET PYQ pattern

questions.question: In the cross AaBbCc × AaBbCc (independent assortment), the proportion of offspring with genotype AaBbcc is

relevance.note: AaBbcc fraction 1/16 in trihybrid – NEET-level genetics

questions.question: A man with blood group A (genotype Iᴬi) marries a woman with blood group B (genotype Iᴮi). The probability that their child has blood group O is
questions.explanation: The child gets i from each parent with probability 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4, giving genotype ii (group O).

relevance.note: IAi × IBi O child 1/4 – NEET staple

questions.question: A double-stranded DNA segment has 1000 base pairs, of which 300 are A–T pairs. The total number of hydrogen bonds between the two strands is
questions.explanation: A–T pairs have 2 H-bonds and G–C pairs 3. 300 × 2 + 700 × 3 = 600 + 2100 = 2700.

relevance.note: H-bond count 2700 from A–T/G–C pairs – NEET style

questions.question: In eukaryotes, the precursor of mRNA (hnRNA) is transcribed by
questions.explanation: RNA polymerase I makes rRNAs (28S, 18S, 5.8S), III makes tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNAs, and II makes hnRNA.

relevance.note: RNA pol II transcribes hnRNA – NEET-level

questions.question: If producers in a food chain fix 10,000 J of energy, how much energy will be available to tertiary consumers according to the 10 per cent law?
questions.explanation: Producers 10,000 J → primary 1000 J → secondary 100 J → tertiary 10 J.

relevance.note: 10% law to tertiary consumer 10 J; trophic-count trap

questions.question: Which of the following animals has an open circulatory system?
questions.explanation: Arthropods such as the cockroach have an open circulatory system; annelids and vertebrates have closed systems.

relevance.note: Cockroach open circulation – NEET-level

questions.question: Which of the following is a pseudocoelomate animal?
questions.explanation: Aschelminthes (roundworms such as Ascaris) are pseudocoelomates. Taenia (flatworm) is acoelomate, Pheretima (annelid) is coelomate and Hydra is diploblastic.

relevance.note: Ascaris pseudocoelomate – NEET staple

questions.question: Inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase by malonate, which closely resembles the substrate succinate, is an example of
questions.explanation: Malonate resembles succinate and competes for the active site of the enzyme: competitive inhibition.

relevance.note: Malonate competitive inhibition – NCERT example, NEET favourite

questions.question: Vital capacity of the lungs is equal to
questions.explanation: Vital capacity = maximum air breathed out after a forced inspiration = ERV + TV + IRV. TV + IRV is inspiratory capacity, RV + ERV is FRC and the sum of all four is total lung capacity.

relevance.note: VC = ERV+TV+IRV – NEET staple

questions.question: In a standard ECG, the QRS complex represents
questions.explanation: The P wave is atrial depolarisation, QRS is ventricular depolarisation and T is ventricular repolarisation.

relevance.note: QRS = ventricular depolarisation – NEET-level

questions.question: Which of the following causes vasodilation and decreases blood pressure, acting as a check on the renin–angiotensin mechanism?
questions.explanation: ANF released by the atrial walls causes vasodilation and lowers blood pressure; angiotensin II and ADH are vasoconstrictors and aldosterone increases Na⁺/water reabsorption.

relevance.note: ANF as check on RAAS – NCERT line NEET asks

questions.question: During contraction of a skeletal muscle fibre, the length of which of the following remains unchanged?
questions.explanation: Thin filaments slide over thick filaments: I-bands and H-zone shorten and the sarcomere shortens, but the A-band (length of thick filaments) stays the same.

relevance.note: A-band unchanged in contraction – NEET staple

questions.question: Which hormone is released from the posterior pituitary?
questions.explanation: The neurohypophysis stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin made by the hypothalamus; the other three are adenohypophysis hormones.

relevance.note: Posterior pituitary oxytocin; NEET-level, plain format

questions.question: Twenty primary oocytes and twenty primary spermatocytes complete gametogenesis. The numbers of ova and sperms formed are respectively
questions.explanation: Each primary oocyte gives one ovum (plus polar bodies) and each primary spermatocyte gives four sperms: 20 ova and 80 sperms.

relevance.note: 20 ova and 80 sperms – NEET gametogenesis count

questions.question: Which of the following is a copper-releasing intrauterine device?
questions.explanation: Multiload 375 (like CuT and Cu7) releases copper ions. Lippes loop is non-medicated; Progestasert and LNG-20 release hormones.

relevance.note: Multiload 375 Cu-IUD – NEET staple

questions.question: The wings of a butterfly and of a bird are
questions.explanation: They perform the same function but have different structure and origin: analogous organs resulting from convergent evolution.

relevance.note: Analogous organs convergent evolution – NEET-level

questions.question: In a population in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium the frequency of a recessive allele is 0.3. The frequency of heterozygous individuals is

relevance.note: 2pq = 0.42 – NEET HW item

questions.question: The infective stage of Plasmodium that enters the human body through the bite of a female Anopheles mosquito is the
questions.explanation: Sporozoites from the mosquito's salivary glands are injected into human blood and first multiply in liver cells.

relevance.note: Sporozoite infective stage – NEET-level

questions.question: A foreign gene is ligated into the BamHI site of the vector pBR322 and used to transform E. coli. The recombinant cells will
options: grow on tetracycline medium but not on ampicillin medium
grow on both ampicillin and tetracycline media
grow on ampicillin medium but not on tetracycline medium
questions.explanation: The BamHI site lies within the tetracycline-resistance gene (tetR). Insertion inactivates tetR while ampR remains functional.

relevance.note: BamHI in tetR – insertional inactivation; NEET concept

questions.question: RNA interference (RNAi) has been used to develop transgenic tobacco plants resistant to
questions.explanation: Nematode-specific genes were introduced to produce dsRNA that silences the specific mRNA of Meloidogyne incognita, protecting tobacco roots. Bt Cry proteins target bollworms and corn borer.

relevance.note: RNAi tobacco vs Meloidogyne incognita – NEET staple

questions.question: A 5 kg block on a rough horizontal surface (coefficient of kinetic friction 0.2) is pulled by a horizontal force of 20 N. Its acceleration is (g = 10 m/s²)

relevance.note: Kinetic friction acceleration 2 m/s² – NEET-level

questions.question: A solid sphere rolls without slipping on a horizontal surface. The ratio of its rotational kinetic energy to its total kinetic energy is
questions.explanation: K_rot = ½(2/5 mR²)ω² = (1/5)mv²; K_total = ½mv² + (1/5)mv² = (7/10)mv². Ratio = (1/5)/(7/10) = 2/7.

relevance.note: Rotational/total KE 2/7 for sphere – NEET PYQ

questions.question: The escape velocity from the Earth is 11.2 km/s. The escape velocity from a planet having twice the mass and twice the radius of the Earth is
questions.explanation: v_e = √(2GM/R) depends on M/R, which is unchanged (2M/2R). So v_e = 11.2 km/s.

relevance.note: Escape speed √(2GM/R) unchanged – NEET scaling trap

questions.question: A small sphere of radius r falling through a viscous liquid attains a terminal velocity v. The terminal velocity of a sphere of the same material with radius 2r in the same liquid is
questions.explanation: Terminal velocity v = 2r²(ρ − σ)g/(9η) ∝ r². Doubling r makes it 4v.

relevance.note: Terminal velocity ∝ r² → 4v – NEET staple

questions.question: An ideal gas undergoes an isothermal expansion. Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: For an ideal gas U depends only on T, so ΔU = 0 at constant T and the first law gives Q = W (heat absorbed equals work done by the gas). Q = 0 describes an adiabatic process; W = 0 an isochoric one.

relevance.note: Isothermal ΔU = 0, Q = W – NEET-level

questions.question: A transverse wave is described by y = 0.02 sin 2π(50t − 0.5x), where x and y are in metres and t in seconds. The speed of the wave is
questions.explanation: ω = 100π rad/s, k = π rad/m. v = ω/k = 100 m/s (equivalently f = 50 Hz, λ = 2 m).

relevance.note: Wave speed from equation 100 m/s – NEET-level

questions.question: Three capacitors of 3 μF each are connected so that two are in parallel and this combination is in series with the third. The equivalent capacitance is
questions.explanation: Parallel pair = 6 μF. In series with 3 μF: (6 × 3)/(6 + 3) = 2 μF.

relevance.note: Capacitor network 2 μF – NEET-level

questions.question: A cell of emf 12 V and internal resistance 1 Ω is connected to an external resistance of 5 Ω. The terminal potential difference of the cell is

relevance.note: Terminal voltage 10 V – NEET-level

questions.question: A galvanometer of resistance 50 Ω gives full-scale deflection for a current of 1 mA. To convert it into a voltmeter of range 0–10 V, one should connect
questions.explanation: R = V/I_g − G = 10/0.001 − 50 = 9950 Ω, connected in series (a parallel shunt makes an ammeter).

relevance.note: Voltmeter conversion 9950 Ω series – NEET staple

questions.question: Two thin lenses of power +5 D and −3 D are placed in contact. The focal length of the combination is
questions.explanation: P = +5 − 3 = +2 D ⇒ f = 1/2 m = +50 cm (converging).

relevance.note: Lens powers combined f = 50 cm – NEET-level

questions.question: Unpolarised light of intensity I₀ passes through two polarisers whose transmission axes are inclined at 60° to each other. The intensity of the emergent light is
questions.explanation: The first polariser transmits I₀/2. Malus’ law at the second: (I₀/2)cos²60° = (I₀/2)(1/4) = I₀/8.

relevance.note: Unpolarised through two polarisers at 60° I0/8 – NEET staple

questions.question: The ratio of the radii of the second and third Bohr orbits of the hydrogen atom is
questions.explanation: rₙ ∝ n², so r₂ : r₃ = 4 : 9.

relevance.note: Bohr radius ∝ n² 4:9 – NEET-level

questions.question: Which logic gate gives an output 1 only when both of its inputs are 0?
questions.explanation: NOR = NOT(A + B) is 1 only for A = B = 0. NAND is 0 only for A = B = 1.

relevance.note: NOR gate truth – NEET-level

questions.question: The conversion of an alkyl chloride into an alkyl iodide by heating with NaI in dry acetone is known as
questions.explanation: In the Finkelstein reaction the NaCl formed is insoluble in dry acetone, driving the halogen exchange forward. Swarts gives alkyl fluorides.

relevance.note: Finkelstein reaction naming – NEET-level

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT give the iodoform test?
questions.explanation: The iodoform test needs a CH₃CO– group or a CH₃CH(OH)– group. Ethanol, acetone and propan-2-ol have it; methanol does not.

relevance.note: Methanol fails iodoform – NEET-level

questions.question: Which of the following species is diamagnetic?
questions.explanation: N₂ has all MOs filled in pairs (bond order 3). O₂ and B₂ each have two unpaired electrons, and NO has one.

relevance.note: N2 diamagnetic vs B2, O2, NO – NEET MOT item

questions.question: For a reaction both ΔH and ΔS are positive. The reaction is spontaneous
questions.explanation: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS becomes negative only when TΔS > ΔH, i.e. above T = ΔH/ΔS.

relevance.note: ΔH, ΔS > 0 spontaneous at high T – NEET-level

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The pH of a 10⁻⁸ M aqueous HCl solution is slightly less than 7.
Reason (R): At such low acid concentration, the H⁺ ions from the ionisation of water cannot be neglected.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: [H⁺] ≈ 10⁻⁸ + ~10⁻⁷ (from water) ≈ 1.05 × 10⁻⁷ M, so pH ≈ 6.98, slightly acidic. A is true and R is exactly why the pH is not 8.

relevance.note: A–R on pH of 1e-8 M HCl – current NEET format and classic trap

questions.question: The average oxidation number of sulphur in sodium tetrathionate (Na₂S₄O₆) is
questions.explanation: 2(+1) + 4x + 6(−2) = 0 ⇒ 4x = 10 ⇒ x = +2.5. (Actually two S are +5 and two are 0.)

relevance.note: S in tetrathionate +2.5 – NEET staple

questions.question: Which of the following 0.1 molal aqueous solutions has the highest boiling point (complete dissociation of electrolytes)?
questions.explanation: ΔTb = iKbm. i = 3 for K₂SO₄, 2 for NaCl and 1 for glucose and urea, so K₂SO₄ has the highest boiling point.

relevance.note: Highest bp via i (K2SO4) – NEET-level

questions.question: The quantity of electricity required to deposit 0.1 mol of aluminium from a solution of Al³⁺ ions is (F = 96500 C mol⁻¹)

relevance.note: 0.3 F for 0.1 mol Al – NEET Faraday item

questions.question: The half-life of a first-order reaction is 10 min. The fraction of the reactant remaining after 30 min is
questions.explanation: 30 min = 3 half-lives; fraction left = (1/2)³ = 1/8.

relevance.note: 1/8 left after 3 half-lives – NEET-level easy

questions.question: Which of the following oxoacids of sulphur contains an S–S bond?
questions.explanation: Thiosulphuric acid has one S bonded directly to the central S. H₂S₂O₇ has an S–O–S bridge, H₂S₂O₈ has an O–O (peroxo) bridge, and H₂SO₄ has a single S.

relevance.note: S–S bond in thiosulphuric acid – NEET oxoacid structure

questions.question: Which of the following ions has the highest spin-only magnetic moment?
questions.explanation: Fe³⁺ (3d⁵) has 5 unpaired electrons (5.92 BM); Cr³⁺ has 3, Cu²⁺ and Ti³⁺ have 1 each.

relevance.note: Fe3+ highest spin-only moment – NEET-level

questions.question: A mixture of o-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol is best separated by
questions.explanation: o-Nitrophenol has intramolecular H-bonding, is steam-volatile and distils with steam; p-nitrophenol is intermolecularly H-bonded and non-volatile.

relevance.note: o/p-nitrophenol steam distillation – NEET staple

questions.question: Which of the following species is aromatic?
questions.explanation: The cyclopentadienyl anion is planar, cyclic and fully conjugated with 6 π electrons (4n + 2, n = 1). The cation has 4 π electrons (antiaromatic), cyclooctatetraene is non-planar with 8, and cycloheptatriene has an sp³ CH₂ breaking conjugation.

relevance.note: Cyclopentadienyl anion aromatic – NEET-level

questions.question: The carbylamine (isocyanide) test is given by
questions.explanation: Heating with CHCl₃ and alcoholic KOH gives foul-smelling isocyanides only with primary (aliphatic or aromatic) amines.

relevance.note: Carbylamine test primary amines only – NEET-level

questions.question: In bryophytes, the main plant body is the
questions.explanation: The dominant, independent phase of bryophytes is the haploid gametophyte; the diploid sporophyte is attached to and dependent on it.

relevance.note: Bryophyte dominant haploid gametophyte – NEET-level

questions.question: Phellogen, phellem and phelloderm are together called
questions.explanation: Cork cambium (phellogen), cork (phellem) and secondary cortex (phelloderm) constitute the periderm. Bark is a non-technical term for all tissues outside the vascular cambium, including secondary phloem.

relevance.note: Periderm composition – NEET-level

questions.question: Diadelphous stamens and vexillary aestivation are characteristic features of the family
questions.explanation: Fabaceae flowers have a standard, wings and keel (vexillary aestivation) and ten stamens arranged in two bundles (9) + 1 — diadelphous. Malvaceae has monadelphous stamens.

relevance.note: Diadelphous + vexillary → Fabaceae – NEET staple

questions.question:
Match List I with List II.
List I: A. Lysosome  B. Ribosome  C. Golgi apparatus  D. Chloroplast
List II: (i) Protein synthesis  (ii) Photosynthesis  (iii) Hydrolytic enzymes  (iv) Formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids
Choose the correct answer.
questions.explanation: Lysosomes contain acid hydrolases; ribosomes are sites of protein synthesis; the Golgi apparatus forms glycoproteins and glycolipids; chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis.

relevance.note: Match-the-list organelle–function in current NEET format

questions.question: A diploid cell has 2C DNA content in G₁ phase. The DNA content after S phase and in each cell formed at the end of meiosis II is respectively
questions.explanation: S phase doubles DNA to 4C (chromosome number unchanged). Meiosis I halves it to 2C per cell and meiosis II to C.

relevance.note: DNA content 4C after S, C after meiosis II – NEET concept

questions.question: In C₄ plants, the primary acceptor of CO₂ in the mesophyll cells is
questions.explanation: PEP carboxylase fixes CO₂ onto the 3-carbon PEP in mesophyll cells, forming the 4-carbon OAA (the first product). RuBP is the acceptor in bundle-sheath cells (Calvin cycle).

relevance.note: PEP primary acceptor in C4 – NEET-level

questions.question: A plant heterozygous for two independently assorting genes (AaBb) is test-crossed with aabb. The expected phenotypic ratio of the progeny is
questions.explanation: AaBb forms four gamete types in equal proportion (AB, Ab, aB, ab); the recessive parent contributes only ab, so the four phenotypes appear 1 : 1 : 1 : 1.

relevance.note: Dihybrid test-cross 1:1:1:1 – NEET-level

questions.question: A typical mature angiosperm embryo sac (Polygonum type) is
questions.explanation: It has 3 antipodals, 2 synergids, 1 egg cell and 1 central cell containing 2 polar nuclei: 7 cells, 8 nuclei.

relevance.note: Embryo sac 7-celled 8-nucleate – NEET staple

questions.question: A colour-blind man marries a woman with normal vision whose father was colour-blind. The probability that a son born to them is colour-blind is
questions.explanation: The woman is a carrier (XᶜX). Sons receive their X from the mother, so half of them get Xᶜ and are colour-blind. (25% is the probability for any child.)

relevance.note: Carrier mother × colour-blind father → sons 50% – NEET pedigree

questions.question: In snapdragon, a cross between true-breeding red-flowered (RR) and white-flowered (rr) plants gives pink-flowered F₁. The phenotypic ratio in the F₂ generation is
questions.explanation: Incomplete dominance: F₂ genotypes RR : Rr : rr = 1 : 2 : 1 each have a distinct phenotype (red : pink : white).

relevance.note: Snapdragon incomplete dominance 1:2:1 – NEET-level

questions.question: A double-stranded DNA molecule contains 20% adenine. The percentage of cytosine in it is
questions.explanation: A = T = 20%, so G + C = 60% and C = G = 30% (Chargaff’s rule).

relevance.note: Chargaff C = 30% – NEET-level

questions.question: In the lac operon of E. coli, the i gene codes for the
questions.explanation: The i (inhibitor) gene codes for the repressor. The structural genes z, y and a code for β-galactosidase, permease and transacetylase.

relevance.note: lac i gene → repressor – NEET-level

questions.question: In the Meselson–Stahl experiment, E. coli grown in ¹⁵NH₄Cl was transferred to ¹⁴NH₄Cl medium. After two generations (about 40 minutes), the DNA extracted would be
options: heavy and light DNA in equal amounts
heavy, hybrid and light DNA in equal amounts
hybrid and light DNA in equal amounts
questions.explanation: Semi-conservative replication: after one generation all DNA is hybrid (¹⁵N/¹⁴N); after the second, half is hybrid and half light (¹⁴N/¹⁴N).

relevance.note: Meselson–Stahl after 2 generations hybrid + light – NEET staple

questions.question: Which ecological pyramid is always upright?
questions.explanation: Energy decreases at each successive trophic level (about 10% transfer), so the energy pyramid can never be inverted. Number and biomass (standing crop) pyramids can be inverted, e.g. a tree ecosystem or the sea.

relevance.note: Pyramid of energy always upright – NEET-level

questions.question: Animals that are radially symmetrical and diploblastic and possess cnidoblasts belong to the phylum
questions.explanation: Cnidarians have stinging cnidoblasts. Ctenophores are also radial and diploblastic but bear comb plates and lack cnidoblasts; sponges have no true tissues; flatworms are bilateral and triploblastic.

relevance.note: Cnidaria by cnidoblasts – NEET-level

questions.question: The inner surface of bronchioles and fallopian tubes is lined by
questions.explanation: Ciliated columnar/cuboidal epithelium moves particles or mucus (bronchioles) and the ovum (fallopian tubes) in a definite direction.

relevance.note: Ciliated epithelium in bronchioles/fallopian tubes – NCERT line

questions.question: In a nucleotide, the nitrogenous base is attached to the pentose sugar by a
questions.explanation: The base joins C-1′ of the sugar through an N-glycosidic bond (forming a nucleoside); phosphate joins via a phosphoester bond, and nucleotides link through phosphodiester bonds.

relevance.note: N-glycosidic linkage base–sugar – NEET-level

questions.question: Approximately what percentage of CO₂ is carried by RBCs as carbamino-haemoglobin?
questions.explanation: NCERT: about 20–25% of CO₂ is carried as carbamino-haemoglobin, about 70% as bicarbonate and about 7% dissolved in plasma. 97% is the figure for O₂ carried by haemoglobin.

relevance.note: 20–25% CO2 as carbamino-Hb – NCERT number NEET asks

questions.question: A healthy person has a heart rate of 72 beats per minute and a stroke volume of 70 mL. The cardiac output is about
questions.explanation: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate = 70 mL × 72 ≈ 5040 mL ≈ 5 L per minute.

relevance.note: Cardiac output ≈ 5 L/min – NEET-level

questions.question:
Statement I: The ascending limb of the loop of Henle is impermeable to water.
Statement II: The descending limb of the loop of Henle is freely permeable to electrolytes.
Choose the correct answer.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation: The ascending limb is impermeable to water but transports electrolytes; the descending limb is permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes. So Statement I is true and Statement II is false.

relevance.note: Statement I/II on loop of Henle permeability – current NEET format

questions.question: The restriction endonuclease EcoRI recognises the sequence
questions.explanation: EcoRI recognises the palindrome 5′-GAATTC-3′ and cuts between G and A on both strands, leaving overhanging sticky ends. GGATCC is the BamHI site.

relevance.note: EcoRI GAATTC sticky ends – NEET-level

questions.question: In the resting state, the axonal membrane is
options: comparatively more permeable to K⁺ and nearly impermeable to Na⁺
more permeable to Na⁺ and nearly impermeable to K⁺
equally permeable to Na⁺ and K⁺
impermeable to both Na⁺ and K⁺
questions.explanation: NCERT: at rest the axolemma is more permeable to K⁺ and nearly impermeable to Na⁺ (and impermeable to the negatively charged proteins of the axoplasm).

relevance.note: Resting membrane permeability K+ > Na+ – NCERT line

questions.question: Addison’s disease is caused by hyposecretion of hormones from the
questions.explanation: Underproduction of glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids by the adrenal cortex causes Addison’s disease (weakness, weight loss, hypotension, pigmentation).

relevance.note: Addison's – adrenal cortex – NEET-level

questions.question: Ovulation in the human menstrual cycle is induced by
questions.explanation: Both LH and FSH peak at mid-cycle, but the rapid LH surge induces rupture of the Graafian follicle and release of the secondary oocyte.

relevance.note: LH surge induces ovulation – NEET-level

questions.question: Which of the following sexually transmitted infections is completely curable if detected early and treated properly?
questions.explanation: NCERT: except hepatitis B, genital herpes and HIV infection, STIs such as gonorrhoea, syphilis and chlamydiasis are completely curable if detected early.

relevance.note: Curable STI gonorrhoea vs viral ones – NEET-level

questions.question: In a population in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, 16% of the individuals show the recessive phenotype. The frequency of the dominant allele is
questions.explanation: q² = 0.16 ⇒ q = 0.4, so p = 1 − 0.4 = 0.6. (0.84 is the frequency of dominant phenotypes and 0.48 that of heterozygotes.)

relevance.note: q² = 0.16 → p = 0.6 with q distractor – NEET HW

questions.question: The antibody present in colostrum that provides passive immunity to the newborn is
questions.explanation: NCERT: colostrum contains abundant IgA antibodies. IgG crosses the placenta, IgE is involved in allergy and IgM appears first in a primary response.

relevance.note: IgA in colostrum – NEET staple

questions.question: During agarose gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments move towards the
options: cathode and separate according to their size
anode and separate according to their base composition
anode and separate according to their size
cathode and separate according to their charge
questions.explanation: DNA is negatively charged, so it migrates towards the anode; the agarose matrix sieves it, so smaller fragments move farther.

relevance.note: Electrophoresis to anode by size – NEET-level

questions.question: The Bt toxin proteins encoded by the genes cryIAc and cryIIAb control
questions.explanation: NCERT: cryIAc and cryIIAb control cotton bollworms, whereas cryIAb controls corn borer. Root-knot nematode resistance was achieved by RNAi.

relevance.note: cryIAc/cryIIAb → cotton bollworm (vs cryIAb corn borer) – NEET favourite
